content.purpose: Defines labels for classifying assertion conflicts (resolution logic not included)

conflict_types.label: Exclusive Conflict
conflict_types.description: Assertions that cannot both be true simultaneously
characteristics: Same subject and predicate with different objects
Only one assertion can be valid
examples: device located_in 'room_a' vs device located_in 'room_b' (if exclusive)
notes: Detection only - no resolution strategy defined

conflict_types.label: Multi-Valued Allowed
conflict_types.description: Multiple assertions with same subject/predicate are valid
examples: person has_name 'Alice' AND person has_name 'Alice Smith' (multiple names)
organization references uri_1 AND organization references uri_2
notes: Indicates no conflict when multiple values present

conflict_types.label: Temporal Conflict
characteristics: Assertions valid in different temporal windows
examples: person located_in 'city_a' @ t1 vs person located_in 'city_b' @ t2
device has_status 'active' @ t1 vs device has_status 'inactive' @ t2

conflict_types.label: Scoped Conflict
examples: dataset has_status 'public' (global scope) vs dataset has_status 'private' (local scope)
person has_name 'Alice' (local) vs person has_name 'Dr. Smith' (global)
notes: Requires scope metadata from Identity Pack

conflict_types.label: Source-Ranked Conflict
conflict_types.description: Assertions from sources with different authority levels
examples: dataset created 'date_a' (user claim) vs dataset created 'date_b' (system record)
person has_name 'X' (external source) vs person has_name 'Y' (authoritative source)
notes: Requires provenance/source metadata not defined in this pack
Detection and classification only - not enforcement
